subject: Post-call: structured-output reliability — decoding constraints & fallback plan
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@finlytics.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + implementation asks — structured output reliability

Alex — thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap (and concrete asks) so we can move toward a short PoC.

Summary (1-line): Finlytics will use Redwood to power a reranker + structured extraction pipeline (embeddings -> reranker -> JSON output for downstream reconciliation) and needs guarantees around structured output correctness and safe fallback behavior.

Open technical asks we discussed:
- SDK & auth: Which SDK language will you use? We support Python/Node/Go — will you use our hosted API key or route through your internal proxy (VPC)?
- Routing: You asked about splitting traffic between a high-precision model for critical reconciliation calls vs a lower-cost model for bulk scoring. Need to confirm percent split and latency SLOs.
- Structured output: You want a stable JSON schema and deterministic keys (transaction_id, suggestion[], confidence). Please attach your canonical schema (we need it to build constrained-decoding + validation hooks).
- Validation & retry patterns: We proposed a two-step approach: 1) constrained decoding + post-parse schema validation; 2) on validation failure, automatic re-sampling with narrower decoding params or fallback to a deterministic extractor. Confirm acceptable retry budget (per-request retries and token budget).

Next steps (mutual action plan):
1) Alex: drop the canonical JSON schema and one sample record set (5–10 items) — we can prototype constrained decoding and validation rules.
2) Ben: draft an implementation plan for SDK init, auth flow options (API key vs signed token), and routing policy to support canary split.
3) Vanessa: prepare a short cost/latency estimate for proposed two-model split and expected token budgets for reranker + extraction.
4) Schedule: propose Wed Aug 18 10:00am PT for a 30m technical sync — please confirm.

Attachments: finlytics-mup-20270815.pdf (MUP/LOB requirements doc) — Alex, you mentioned there is an internal schema; dropping that would be helpful.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + implementation asks — structured output reliability

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers and I attached our working schema (response-schema-v1.json) in this thread.

Answers:
- SDK: our backend team will prototype in Python first; we can run a short PoC from our AWS account. We prefer Redwood hosted API keys initially, but if we can run through a VPC/Private route later that would be ideal for production.
- Traffic split: start with 10% high-precision (higher-cost) model, 90% cheaper model; target p95 latency for web UI use is < 250ms. Bulk offline batch scoring can be 1–2s.
- Retry budget: acceptable to have up to 2 automatic retries per request (different seed/temperature) if schema validation fails; after that fall back to a deterministic extractor with a warning flag back to Finlytics.

Notes about schema: we require that transaction_id is never mutated, and suggestion[] must include an id and source_token_span when provided. We'll attach 5 sample records in the Drive link.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/finlytics/specs/response-schema-v1
Attached: response-schema-v1.json

On Wed Aug 18 10:00am PT works for the technical sync.

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + implementation asks — structured output reliability

Alex/Jonas — thanks, schema received. I've drafted a pragmatic implementation approach below focused on reliability + minimal engineering lift for the PoC.

High-level approach (PoC):
1) SDK init & auth
   - Use Redwood Python SDK with hosted API key for PoC. We'll provide snippet to rotate keys and set scoped usage (dev vs prod).
   - For production, recommend our Private route (customer-managed VPC) + short-lived signed tokens to avoid shipping long-lived keys.

2) Routing
   - Implement a traffic-split policy in the Redwood control plane: 10% -> model-a (high-precision), 90% -> model-b (cost-optimized).
   - Canary deploy capability: we'll tag a subset of users via request metadata to verify before full rollout.

3) Structured output reliability (core of this thread)
   A) Constrained decoding: use our schema-guided decoder that enforces required keys and basic types during generation. This reduces malformed JSON by ~85% in our benchmarks.
   B) Post-parse validation: run a JSON schema validator (we'll include a node/python validator snippet) to enforce cardinality and types, and to validate non-mutation of transaction_id.
   C) Retry pattern: on validation failure -> trigger automatic re-sample with: lower temperature, higher top_p narrowing, and stronger token-by-token constraints for up to 2 retries. Each retry will log full request/response to the MUP (masked for PII).
   D) Final fallback: if retries fail, run deterministic extractor (rule-based regex + lightweight span model) and attach a warning flag (schema_validation: "fallback_used"). This ensures downstream reconciliation still receives structured data.

4) Embeddings & reranker integration
   - Keep the embedding vector + doc-id mapping intact through the pipeline. Our suggestion: return suggestion[].id that maps directly to your doc-id and include a source_token_span when available.

Telemetry & audit
- We'll emit per-request validation status, retry_count, model_used, and latency. These will appear in the Redwood Console per-route dashboard.

PoC deliverables (week 1):
- Snippets: Python SDK init, auth, and sample request for constrained decoding
- Example validator: response-schema-v1.json + validator script
- Routing policy config for 10/90 split and canary tag snippet

Questions for Finlytics:
- Can you confirm how important strict deterministic outputs are for the UI vs offline reconciliation? If UI requires perfect stability, we should increase the high-precision traffic or consider a sync-side deterministic extractor path.
- Please confirm sample size for PoC (Ben asked for 5–10 records — Alex already said 5).

I attached a quick validator example and will push code snippets to the Drive link after this email.

Ben Carter
Principal Product Engineer | Redwood Inference
